verdict: Copart grew revenue 2.4% to $1,152M, but higher yard costs cut gross profit 5.5% and net income fell 17% to $327M.

kpis.label: Service revenues
kpis.note: +1.4% YoY — auction fees are 84% of revenue (shown as $969M in the flow; see footer)

kpis.label: Gross profit
kpis.note: -5.5% YoY — facility costs rose much faster than sales

segments.name: Service revenues
segments.note: Fees for running online auctions of damaged and unwanted vehicles, mostly for insurance companies. Copart reports $970M; it is shown here as $969M so the rounded segments sum exactly to total revenue.

segments.name: Vehicle sales
segments.note: Vehicles Copart buys itself and resells at auction, rather than selling for someone else. Up 8.3%.

opex.name: General and administrative
opex.note: Copart splits this into general and administrative of $97M, plus $7M of depreciation and amortization and $8M of stock-based compensation in general and administrative.

otherDetail: Other income was $36M, net: $40M of interest income, net, partly offset by $4M of other expense, net.

takeaways.title: Sales edged up
takeaways.text: Revenue rose 2.4% to $1,152M. Service revenues — the auction fees that are the core business — rose 1.4% to $970M, while vehicle sales rose 8.3% to $183M.

takeaways.title: Costs squeezed the yards' margin
takeaways.text: Gross margin fell from 45.3% to 41.8%. Facility (yard) operations cost $451M, up 7.7%, and the cost of vehicles Copart itself bought and resold rose 11.4% — both far faster than revenue. Gross profit fell 5.5% to $481M despite higher sales.

takeaways.title: Profit fell even as sales rose
takeaways.text: Net income fell 17% to $327M and EPS fell to $0.35 from $0.41. Higher yard and admin costs did most of the damage, and other income also dropped from $66M to $36M as interest income fell 21%.

footerNote: Reports in thousands; figures are rounded to $M. Cost of revenue here is every facility cost above the gross-profit line in Copart's statement.
follow100Note: The facility costs in cost of revenue are yard operations $451M, cost of vehicle sales $164M, facility depreciation and amortization $54M and facility stock-based compensation $2M. Service revenues are shown at $969M (reported $970M) and general and administrative at $97M (reported $98M) so the rounded lines tie exactly. Consolidated net income was $327M; a $1M loss (rounded) attributable to noncontrolling interests means net income attributable to Copart was also $327M.
